content: Wonder is an emotional state that shares similarities with surprise, as it is most frequently experienced when encountering something rare or unexpected. However, unlike surprise, wonder is distinctly positive in its emotional tone and can persist for extended durations. This emotion has been specifically associated with curiosity and the motivation to pursue scientific inquiry. René Descartes identified wonder as one of the fundamental emotions, asserting that emotions, in general, are responses to unexpected phenomena. Wonder is also often compared to the emotion of awe, which encompasses moral, spiritual, and aesthetic dimensions. Jonathan Haidt (2003) explored awe as a moral, spiritual, and aesthetic emotion in his work published in Cognition and Emotion. Additionally, Haidt and Dacher Keltner (2004) examined the appreciation of beauty and excellence in their contribution to the book Character Strengths and Virtues, edited by Christopher Peterson and Martin E.P. Seligman, published by the American Psychological Association Press. Their discussion spans pages 537 to 551.
